chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Goodman's band and how Wilson was hired for the trio
summary: Wilson recalls Goodman's rise, the Congress Hotel Sunday concerts in Chicago, and Hammond getting Goodman to keep him; the trio then grew to a quartet with Hampton.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: And then, from there, I got a call from Goodman -- Goodman had become a bandleader during 1935 and with a regular show sponsored by the National Biscuit Company, a three-hour radio program, and when that went off the air, he kept the band together, because the band was only organized for the radio, but he kept it together and they performed at the Billy Rose Music Hall in New York, and then he took the band on the road. And the backbone of the writing was Benny Carter and Fletcher Henderson in those days. That was the
original Goodman big band style. And the band toured the country and flopped all the way down the line and finally made a big hit in Los Angeles, at the Paramount Ballroom.

And then on their swing back east, they stopped at the Congress Hotel in Chicago for a long run, and they started having Sunday afternoon jazz concerts, and guests beside the Benny Goodman band playing the afternoon program, and they brought me out from New York from the Famous Door -- I took leave one Sunday afternoon, and that was when John Hammond got Goodman to hire me and keep me on, and I never did go back to the Famous Door.
I stayed with Goodman with the trio for a year.
And then later on, Lionel Hampton joined the small group as a quartet and that continued with me until 1939, and I left to form a big band of my own.
